conceptual.title: Level 1 — Core ML Concepts
conceptual.description: Covers key theoretical and algorithmic foundations from lectures and annotated notes.
questions: What is the difference between training error and generalization error, and why can relying solely on training error be misleading?
Explain the bias-variance tradeoff in the context of model evaluation. How does it relate to overfitting and underfitting?
Describe the main steps of backpropagation and how gradient descent updates the network weights.
What are the advantages of cross-validation compared to using a single validation set?
How do kernel methods enable non-linear decision boundaries while still using linear models?

applied.title: Level 2 — Applied Algorithms and Model Design
applied.description: Focuses on applying ML algorithms and comparing modeling strategies from assignments and lecture materials.
questions: What are the main differences between linear regression, logistic regression, and perceptron models? In what scenarios would each be appropriate?
How does ridge regression prevent overfitting, and how does its loss function differ from ordinary least squares?
Explain the idea behind K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and discuss one advantage and one limitation of this algorithm.
Compare Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and XGBoost in terms of interpretability and performance trade-offs for policy data prediction.
What role do cosponsorship and fiscal data play in predicting the likelihood of a bill's enactment in your project?

project.title: Level 3 — Integration and Reflection
project.description: Links ML theory with your final project on legislative bill prediction and reflection on model design choices.
questions: How can feature selection techniques improve your model's predictive performance when using legislative text data?
Discuss how embedding-based similarity could be applied to classify bills with similar policy intent.
Why is model interpretability important in policy prediction contexts? Give one example from the Illinois legislature project.
In the project, which machine learning model performed best, and why?
If I was to extend the project to other states or national bills, what modifications would you recommend me to make to improve generalization?
